channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Four Afghan Youths Die on Migration Route, Buried in Samangan
item.description: Four young men from Samangan province died while migrating through Türkiye and Iran seeking economic opportunities. Their bodies were returned from Kabul for burial. A relative alleged Turkish border forces' beatings caused their deaths. Families urge UN and Islamic Emirate to investigate.

item.title: New $1.63 Billion Road to Connect Southern and Western Kazakhstan with Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Development Bank approved financing for a new republican road connecting Ulygaysyn and Saksauylsk, linking southern and western Kazakhstan, as well as Uzbekistan, to Russia. The $1.63 billion project aims to enhance logistics between Europe and Asia, creating over 10,000 jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Expand Air Traffic with Germany Under New Agreement
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to expand its air traffic with Germany, with a new agreement being prepared. The country's airlines currently operate 65 Airbus aircraft, and expect 23 more by 2030. Discussions also covered cooperation with Airbus on fleet development.

item.title: IMF Warns Kazakhstan: State Megaprojects Could Fuel New Inflationary Spiral
item.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has issued a warning to Kazakhstan, indicating that large-scale state-sponsored megaprojects carry the risk of triggering a new wave of inflation. The fund advises caution regarding the potential economic consequences of these ambitious development initiatives.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts 45th Plenary Meeting of Eurasian Group on Combating Money Laundering
item.description: Dushanbe is hosting the 45th plenary meeting of the Eurasian Group (EAG) on combating money laundering and terrorism financing, running from November 16 to November 20. Working groups convened on November 16 to discuss mutual evaluations, legal issues, technical assistance, and typologies of financial crime.

item.title: Almaty to Build New Factories and Energy Facilities with 142 Billion Tenge Investment
item.description: Almaty plans to implement investment projects totaling 142 billion tenge, including the construction of new factories and energy infrastructure. These projects are expected to create approximately 950 new jobs and will focus on sectors like energy, industry, and tourism, enhancing the city's economic landscape.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allocates Over 19 Billion Som for Irrigation Infrastructure Development
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated over 19 billion som from the national budget for irrigation infrastructure development between 2021 and 2026. These funds are being used to construct and renovate 112 water management facilities, aiming to improve water supply for agricultural lands and boost agricultural production and exports.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry Holds Billions in Victim Compensation Fund
item.description: Billions of tenge are accumulating in Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance's Victim Compensation Fund, with only 685 individuals receiving payouts in 2026. The ministry states it merely collects funds, while law enforcement and investigative bodies are responsible for determining recipients and victim lists. The fund holds 8.8 billion tenge, with 2.2 billion received in the first ten months of 2026.

item.title: Russia Reports Third Ukrainian Attack on Crimean Bridge This Week
item.description: Crimea's Moscow-appointed head, Sergei Aksyonov, reported a third Ukrainian attack on the Crimean Bridge this week, leading to temporary traffic suspension. The bridge had previously suffered severe damage from two earlier attacks. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy described the initial attacks as an "unprecedented operation" prepared over weeks.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Rules for Drug Testing Civil Servants
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved new regulations allowing civil servants to be tested for drug use based on behavioral and physical signs. Indicators include frequent lateness, red eyes, drowsiness, loss of interest in work, mood swings, and poor hygiene. Supervisors will observe employees for these signs, which could lead to mandatory medical examination.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 7 Billion Som for 3% Loans to Develop Livestock Farming
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to allocate 7 billion som by 2027 for preferential 3% loans to develop livestock farming. Myktybek Kalandarov, head of the Livestock and Veterinary Department, stated that 1.232 billion som has already been disbursed this year for purchasing pedigree animals. An additional 270 million som is expected soon for farmers wishing to acquire pedigree livestock.

item.title: Trump Reiterates Decision to Go to War with Iran Despite Political Costs
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated he would still choose to go to war with Iran if faced with the same circumstances again, despite acknowledging potential political consequences. He described past negotiations mediated by Islamabad as a "waste of time," deeming Iranian officials untrustworthy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Support for Women Entrepreneurs to Grow Small Businesses
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is implementing measures to expand women's participation in business and support their development. The UN Women representative highlighted the role of state-provided conditions, including preferential loans at 0-6% annual interest. A memorandum was signed to foster cooperation in developing women's entrepreneurship.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Rules for Bank Restructuring and Depositor Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved new procedures for restructuring banks facing financial difficulties. The rules aim to protect depositors, ensure uninterrupted banking services, and improve financial sector problem-solving. Assets and liabilities can be transferred to another bank, or a temporary bank may be established. Depositor funds are protected from write-offs or conversion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize Over 510 Million Tenge Worth of Contraband Cigarettes and Vapes
item.description: Kazakhstan's border guards have seized contraband cigarettes and vapes valued at over 510 million tenge. In the Aktobe and Zhambyl regions, authorities intercepted 593,000 packs of cigarettes and nearly 14,000 vapes attempting to cross the border illegally. The KNB has transferred the cases to investigative bodies.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Unemployment Benefits Amount Starting 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will change the procedure for receiving unemployment benefits. The maximum monthly payment will increase to 346,500 tenge, calculated as 45% of the average monthly income over the last two years, capped at 45% of seven minimum wages. The duration of benefits will also be adjusted based on social contribution history.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Fines for Unauthorized Publication of Officials' Private Photos
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a proposal to restrict the publication of private photos and videos of officials without their consent. Lawmaker Maxim Rozhin suggests prohibiting the dissemination of images taken during officials' leisure, family, or religious events. This aims to distinguish between public service and private life. Fines could reach up to 129,750 tenge for individuals and 865,000 tenge for organizations.

item.title: 189 Kyrgyz Citizens Detained at Russia's Sakharovo Migration Center
item.description: As of November 17, 189 citizens of Kyrgyzstan, including 33 women, are being held at Russia's 'Sakharovo' temporary detention center for foreign nationals. The Kyrgyz Ombudsman's Institute reported that Ombudsman Jamila Jamanbaeva visited the center to assess detention conditions, medical care, and rights protection. Migrants were advised on Russian laws and how to protect their rights.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Monthly Benefits for Children with Disabilities from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, monthly benefits for children with disabilities in Kyrgyzstan will increase from 8,000 to 11,000 soms. This is part of the state's social policy, as announced by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Other benefits for orphans and mothers will also be raised.

item.title: Kazakhstan Urges Global Response to Terrorist Threats Emanating from Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi stated that developments in Afghanistan and extremist networks pose regional stability threats. He called for international coordination at the Schuman Security and Defence Forum. Kazakhstan reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Afghanistan's economic and humanitarian development.

item.title: Bishkek Fines Taxi Drivers for Operating Without Licenses Near Alamedin Market
item.description: Bishkek authorities conducted a raid near Alamedin market, fining taxi drivers for operating without proper licenses. The operation, involving municipal and police units, aimed to curb illegal passenger transportation. Fines were issued, though specific numbers were not disclosed.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Establish Joint Research Institute for Alatau City Development
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are launching a joint Smart City research institute to develop the city of Alatau using modern technologies. An agreement was signed between Kazakh and Chinese institutions, focusing on scientific research and technological development for urban infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Special Auto Loan Rules, Raising Concerns Over Debt
item.description: Kazakh banks will have an additional year to issue certain auto loans without adhering to standard borrower debt load limits. This measure may boost car sales but could also increase the number of non-performing loans. An economist expressed concerns about the decision and its potential impact on the auto market.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Prepares for Presidential Election: Key Candidates and Their Hopes
item.description: Preparations are underway for Kyrgyzstan's presidential election scheduled for January 27, 2027. The initial phase, including candidate registration and signature collection, is ongoing. President Sadyr Japarov met with potential candidates, assuring equal conditions and no use of administrative resources. The Central Election Commission is verifying readiness.

item.title: Uzbek Professor Sentenced to 10 Years in Kazakhstan for Espionage
item.description: A 46-year-old Uzbek citizen, professor Ikboljon Karabaev, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison in Kazakhstan after being found guilty of espionage. The trial was held in camera due to classified information. Karabaev taught international relations at a university in Astana and was reportedly detained in July.

item.title: Xi Jinping Urges APEC Nations to Accelerate Free Trade Zone Negotiations
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) countries to intensify negotiations on establishing a regional free trade zone. He emphasized removing trade and investment barriers and announced China's $20 million contribution to support practical cooperation within APEC.

item.title: Kumtor Gold Mine: Five Key Decisions Made Over Five Years
item.description: More than five years have passed since the "Kumtor Gold Company" CJSC came under state management. During this period, a series of strategically important decisions were adopted concerning the mine's operations and future.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Receives Kazakhstan's Ambassador
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with Kazakhstan's Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Abylkair Skakov. They discussed promising directions for Kyrgyz-Kazakh cooperation in political, trade-economic, transit-transport, and cultural-humanitarian spheres, focusing on modernizing border crossing points.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan May Reintroduce Visa-Free Travel for Border Residents
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are planning to resume flights and simplify visa procedures, according to Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Discussions included transport links, border crossings, and visa-free movement for residents of border areas. The countries also considered resuming direct flights between Tashkent and Ashgabat.

item.title: Crimean Bridge Hit for Third Time This Week in Reported Ukrainian Attack
item.description: Traffic across the Crimean Bridge was suspended following a reported Ukrainian attack, the third strike this week. Russian-installed official Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the incident. Previous attacks caused significant structural damage to the roadway and railway sections.

item.title: Opponent of Janibek Alimkhanuly, Jacob Bank, Faces Suspicions of Doping Use
item.description: Danish boxer Jacob Bank, scheduled to fight Janibek Alimkhanuly, is suspected of using banned substances. A Russian YouTube channel author raised doubts about Bank's physical conditioning, suggesting potential use of performance-enhancing drugs. Bank is set to challenge for a vacant WBO middleweight title in January 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Banning Online Platform Registration for Children Under 16
item.description: Kazakhstan's Parliament has approved draft laws in their first reading that propose prohibiting children under 16 from registering on online platforms. The proposed amendments also introduce new requirements for digital services and increase accountability for online violations. Messenger services intended for interpersonal communication would be exempt from the ban.

item.title: New Bishkek Warehouse to Increase Vaccine Storage Capacity to 200,000 Doses
item.description: A new vaccine storage facility in Bishkek will significantly expand capacity from 14-20,000 doses to 200,000 doses. This upgrade will reduce transportation costs and ensure modern storage standards for vaccines. The facility is equipped with refrigerators maintaining positive and negative temperature regimes, and an air conditioning system.

item.title: BRICS New Development Bank Lends Uzbekistan $300 Million for Renewable Energy
item.description: Uzbekistan has secured a $300 million loan from the BRICS New Development Bank (NDB) to finance solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear power generation. This initiative aims to meet growing energy demand, reduce reliance on natural gas, and enhance energy security and environmental commitments. The Ministry of Economy and Finance will coordinate the project.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Elderly Face Poverty Despite High Employment Rates
item.description: A report indicates that 48.4% of Kyrgyz citizens aged 60-64 are still working, and 71.6% of those over 55 financially support family. However, nearly one in five elderly citizens live below the poverty line, with significant regional disparities. Healthcare costs also strain budgets for elderly-only households.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Electronic Platform for Interbank Cash Distribution
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved new rules for banks managing cash, including the creation of an electronic platform for distributing cash between financial institutions. This system will allow banks with excess cash to offer it to others, and those in need to submit electronic requests. The Ministry of Justice has registered the procedure.

item.title: Illegal River Diversion in Jetisu Region Halted by Authorities
item.description: Authorities in the Jetisu region have stopped illegal activities by unauthorized prospectors who altered the course of the Karatal River. The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation reported that the diversion, conducted without proper state consent, could disrupt the river's hydrological regime and cause flooding. Administrative measures have been applied to the violators.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan National Bank Mandates Capital Increase for Banks with Foreign Branches
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has introduced new capital requirements for commercial banks operating or planning to open branches abroad. Banks must increase their charter capital by at least 3% of their foreign branch's assets after the first year, and subsequently by 3% of asset growth. These regulations, effective November 12, 2026, aim to strengthen financial stability.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Recommends Loan for Small Hydropower Plant Construction
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has recommended Eldik Bank provide a loan for the construction of a small hydropower plant in Mailuu-Suu, Jalal-Abad region. The bank may finance 70% of the contract value in Chinese yuan at 6% annual interest over ten years. The project aims to ensure reliable electricity supply to the city and surrounding areas.

item.title: Organized Extortion Group Arrested in Tashkent
item.description: An organized criminal group suspected of numerous extortion crimes has been apprehended in Tashkent. The group allegedly interfered in private debt disputes, using violence and intimidation to "resolve" issues and seize funds. Several individuals, including a previously convicted leader, were detained.
